patient.name: Marcus Delgado
patient.chiefComplaint: Motor vehicle collision with abdominal pain and lightheadedness

history.hpi: Restrained driver in a single-vehicle collision, moderate front-end intrusion, airbag deployed. Patient is alert but reports diffuse abdominal pain and lightheadedness when the stretcher head is raised. No loss of consciousness reported. Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
history.events: Vehicle struck a guardrail after swerving to avoid debris; bystanders called 911 immediately, patient was found still restrained in the driver's seat

scene.dispatch: 28-year-old male, single-vehicle motor vehicle collision, patient conscious, guardrail involved
scene.location: Two-lane rural highway shoulder, vehicle with moderate front-end damage against a guardrail
scene.safety: Vehicle stable, engine off, traffic control established by law enforcement on scene
scene.bystanders: Passing motorist stopped and called 911, did not witness the moment of impact
visualCues: Moderate front-end vehicle damage with deployed airbag
Patient pale and diaphoretic, restrained in driver's seat
Steering wheel deformity consistent with abdominal contact
Patient's arms show faint, thready peripheral veins on visual inspection

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 28-year-old male restrained in the driver's seat, alert but pale and diaphoretic, reporting diffuse abdominal pain. Vital signs reveal early compensated shock from suspected intra-abdominal hemorrhage.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak and thready bilaterally, skin pale and cool
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities
otherFindings: Diffuse abdominal tenderness, worse in the left upper quadrant
Steering wheel-pattern contusion across the abdomen
Lightheadedness when stretcher head is elevated
Peripheral veins visibly constricted and difficult to palpate on both forearms
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "My stomach really hurts... I feel kind of dizzy."

transitions.if: IO placed after failed IV attempts
transitions.condition: Crew performs the MARCH primary survey, recognizes signs of hemorrhagic shock, attempts peripheral IV access twice without success on vasoconstricted veins, and transitions to IO access within the protocol's 90-second/two-attempt threshold.
Crew continues attempting peripheral IV access beyond two attempts or 90 seconds instead of transitioning to IO, delaying fluid resuscitation while the patient's shock progresses.

phases.name: IO placed after failed IV attempts
phases.description: After two unsuccessful peripheral IV attempts on severely vasoconstricted veins, the crew places a humeral IO and begins fluid resuscitation while continuing serial reassessment for occult hemorrhage.
phases.triggerCondition: After two peripheral IV attempts fail within roughly 90 seconds due to vasoconstriction from compensated shock, the crew recognizes further peripheral attempts are unlikely to succeed and places an IO needle per the shock protocol's access threshold.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: IO catheter secured in proximal humerus, flushing without infiltration
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities
otherFindings: IO successfully placed after two failed peripheral attempts
500 mL isotonic fluid bolus infusing under pressure
Abdominal tenderness unchanged, no new findings
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That pinch in my arm... okay, that's a little better now."

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform MARCH primary survey: hemorrhage, airway, breathing, circulation, head/hypothermia
expectedActions.rationale: Identifies life threats and directs the crew toward recognizing occult hemorrhagic shock.

expectedActions.shortAction: Place IO after 2 failed peripheral IV attempts (or >90 sec) on vasoconstricted veins
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle
expectedActions.rationale: Compensated shock causes peripheral vasoconstriction that makes standard IV access unreliable; IO gives immediate reliable access.

expectedActions.shortAction: Give 500 mL isotonic fluid bolus via IO for SBP <90 mmHg with HR >100
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If SBP less than 90 mmHg or HR greater than 120 BPM, initiate resuscitation: ... consider 500 mL bolus of IV fluid, repeat as needed for persistent signs and symptoms of shock
expectedActions.rationale: Restores perfusion toward the trauma resuscitation target while definitive hemorrhage control is arranged.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess SBP and mental status after fluid bolus
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms response to fluids and guides whether additional boluses are needed.

transitions.condition: IO access secured, fluid resuscitation underway, and patient is packaged with continued serial reassessment for rapid transport to an appropriate trauma center.

phases.name: Packaged for rapid transport
phases.description: With IO access established and fluid resuscitation underway, the patient is packaged and rapidly transported to an appropriate trauma center, with ongoing serial vital sign reassessment for evolving hemorrhagic shock.
phases.triggerCondition: After IO placement and initial fluid bolus improve perfusion, the crew minimizes scene time and initiates rapid transport given the suspected intra-abdominal hemorrhage.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: IO patent, fluids infusing, distal pulses improving
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all four extremities
otherFindings: Abdominal tenderness persistent, unchanged in distribution
Lightheadedness resolved with head of stretcher flat
Patient packaged and secured for transport
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I still feel it in my stomach, but I'm not as dizzy anymore."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vitals and neuro status serially en route; monitor for occult hemorrhage
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Monitor patient for deterioration over time with serial vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) and repeat neurologic status assessment. Patients with compensated shock may not manifest hypotension until severe blood loss has occurred
expectedActions.rationale: Compensated shock can mask ongoing intra-abdominal hemorrhage until decompensation occurs suddenly.

expectedActions.shortAction: Minimize scene time (<10 min) and transport to appropriate trauma center per field triage guideline
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Target scene time less than 10 minutes for unstable patients or those likely to need surgical intervention. Decisions regarding transport destination should be based on the ACS-COT 2022 National Guideline for the Field Triage of Injured Patients
expectedActions.rationale: Suspected intra-abdominal hemorrhage requires rapid surgical evaluation at an appropriate trauma center.

phases.name: Peripheral attempts continue past threshold
phases.description: The crew continues attempting peripheral IV access beyond the two-attempt/90-second threshold instead of transitioning to IO. Fluid resuscitation is delayed and the patient's compensated shock begins to decompensate.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew persists with additional peripheral IV attempts on severely vasoconstricted veins well past the protocol's threshold, delaying any fluid administration while perfusion continues to worsen.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses now absent, palpable only at carotid/femoral
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact but patient increasingly lethargic
otherFindings: No vascular access obtained after repeated peripheral attempts

expectedActions.shortAction: Stop peripheral attempts now; place IO immediately and begin fluid bolus
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle
expectedActions.rationale: Continued delay in obtaining access allows uncompensated shock to progress; IO must be placed without further delay.
